content: 1. Positron emission tomography (PET) using 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) has been systematically reviewed and analyzed for its diagnostic utility in detecting cervical node metastases in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. This imaging modality has shown significant potential in improving diagnostic accuracy. (Eur J Cancer, 2014) 2. A meta-analysis conducted in 2008 demonstrated the effectiveness of FDG-PET in evaluating cervical lymph node metastases in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma patients, highlighting its role in staging and treatment planning. (J Natl Cancer Inst, 2008) 3. A prospective study evaluated the use of FDG-PET/CT in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma who presented with negative findings on neck palpation. The study emphasized the sensitivity of PET/CT in identifying occult metastases. (Radiology, 2014) 4. Combined FDG-PET and computed tomography (CT) have been proposed as a primary screening method for detecting second primary cancers and distant metastases in head and neck cancer patients, with studies supporting its utility in comprehensive cancer management. (Ann Oncol, 2007) 5. A meta-analysis published in 2011 assessed the role of FDG-PET/CT in detecting distant metastases and second primary cancers in head and neck cancer patients, reinforcing its value in advanced diagnostic protocols. (Oral Oncol, 2011) 6. Limitations of FDG-PET in detecting early synchronous primary cancers in untreated head and neck squamous cell carcinoma patients have been noted, suggesting the need for complementary diagnostic approaches. (Ann Nucl Med, 2013) 7. Retrospective image fusion of FDG-PET and MRI has been compared with PET/CT and contrast-enhanced neck MRI for preoperative staging of head and neck cancer, demonstrating the potential benefits of multimodal imaging. (Eur J Radiol, 2013) 8. Intralaryngeal ultrasonography has been clinically assessed for its diagnostic value in laryngeal and laryngopharyngeal cancers, providing a non-invasive imaging option for tumor evaluation. (Laryngoscope, 2001) 9. Diagnostic procedures for detecting lymph node metastases in laryngeal cancer have been extensively reviewed, with emphasis on the importance of accurate nodal staging in treatment planning. (ORL J Otorhinolaryngol Relat Spec, 2000) 10. The utility of sonography in evaluating clinical T1 and T2 glottic carcinoma has been explored, with findings supporting its role in early-stage tumor assessment. (J Ultrasound Med, 2009) 11. Comparative studies between sonography and non-contrast-enhanced MRI for assessing glottic squamous cell carcinoma have highlighted the strengths and limitations of each modality. (J Ultrasound Med, 2011) 12. Preoperative risk assessment in elective general surgery has been discussed, emphasizing the importance of evaluating comorbidities and optimizing patient outcomes. (Br J Surg, 1996) 13. The 2014 ACC/AHA guidelines on perioperative cardiovascular evaluation and management for non-cardiac surgery patients provide a comprehensive framework for risk stratification and intervention. (Circulation, 2014) 14. The impact of preoperative comprehensive geriatric assessment on postoperative outcomes in older patients undergoing scheduled surgery has been systematically reviewed, underscoring its significance in surgical care. (Anaesthesia, 2014) 15. The diagnosis and preoperative work-up of laryngeal cancer have been detailed, with a focus on optimizing surgical and non-surgical treatment strategies. (Otolaryngol Clin North Am, 2008) 16. Perioperative medical management of patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has been reviewed, highlighting strategies to minimize complications and improve surgical outcomes. (Int J Chron Obstruct Pulmon Dis, 2007) 17. Factors predicting postoperative pulmonary complications after supracricoid partial laryngectomy have been identified, aiding in risk assessment and patient counseling. (Arch Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg, 2009) 18. Preoperative evaluation for partial laryngectomy has been discussed, emphasizing the importance of thorough assessment to ensure optimal surgical outcomes. (Head Neck Surg, 1988) 19. The incidence of second primary malignancies in patients treated for head and neck cancer has been comprehensively reviewed, with implications for long-term surveillance and management. (Curr Med Res Opin, 2012) 20. Synchronous and metachronous head and neck carcinomas have been analyzed, providing insights into their clinical behavior and implications for treatment planning. (Cancer, 1994) 21. Current opinions on the diagnosis and treatment of laryngeal carcinoma have been reviewed, with a focus on advancements in surgical and non-surgical approaches. (Cancer Treat Rev, 2006) 22. The role of FDG-PET in the initial staging of nodal-negative oral and oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma has been evaluated, with findings supporting its use in specific clinical scenarios. (Head Neck, 2002) 23. Detection of synchronous primary tumors in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma using FDG-PET/CT has been studied, demonstrating its utility in comprehensive cancer evaluation. (Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging, 2009) 24. False-negative findings for primary lung tumors on FDG-PET have been reported, with implications for staging and prognosis in head and neck cancer patients. (AJR Am J Roentgenol, 2004) 25. The synchronous, multicentric, and metachronous nature of head and neck cancers has been explored, providing a framework for understanding tumor biology and progression. (Head Neck Surg, 1988)
